contradictions.detail: The listing intro and BaT Essentials say 18in Style 261M wheels. The wheel paragraph says 17in Style 261M. The seller says they came from an LCI 135i. The window sticker shows factory 17in star-spoke wheels.

critical_evidence.evidence: The detailed work list (VANOS, gaskets, timing-chain tensioner, belt, mounts, plugs) never mentions the electric water pump, thermostat, expansion tank or coolant hoses. At 153k miles these are a known N52 failure point. No reported entry means we do not know; it is not proof they were never replaced.

The listing reports replaced oil pan, valve cover, oil-filter-housing, intake and valvetronic gaskets, and says parts/service records are included. The receipts are not examined here. Photos show a clean engine bay and an apparently dry undertray, but not the pan or housing directly.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is strong: VIN matches the window sticker, Carfax summary with 27 records, clean-title claim and disclosed accident. The maintenance half is referenced but not examined: records and FCP receipts are said to exist. The cooling-system history, the model's key weak point, is absent.

condition.rationale: The photos show a clean engine bay, an apparently dry undertray, decent tires and a tidy interior with some bolster wear. Brakes were reportedly done in 2024 and extensive oil-gasket and VANOS work claimed. Stated defects: cracked paint on the right quarter, a skirt scrape, hood chips and dings, plus a replaced fender. The car has 153k miles, Northeast history and unknown cooling-system status.

price_value.rationale: Fair value is estimated at $9,716–$10,850. With 324 watchers and enthusiastic comments, the hammer will likely land at or above that. Known work is modest: CA exhaust/intake reversion and cosmetic paint. An undocumented water pump is a likely near-term cost.

mission_fit.rationale: This is the profile's primary bridge target: a manual, naturally aspirated N52 rear-drive coupe, likely well under the ideal price band and easy to resell. The unknown cooling history matters specifically after the 335i's coolant failure.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Connecticut, far from Carmel. PPI access is not stated, though the seller is responsive and there are 5 days left. BaT shipping or a fly-and-drive is possible. CA smog is feasible once the factory muffler and airbox are refitted.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits together: six-speed manual, Montego Blue over Terracotta, slicktop, non-nav dash, and tasteful OEM-plus M Sport parts. The muffler delete is a reversible taste item.

ppi_focus: Electric water pump and thermostat: scan the pump's operating data, pressure-test the cooling system, and inspect the expansion tank and hoses.
Re-check for oil seepage at the oil-filter housing, valve cover, oil pan and the 135i oil-cooler lines in the passenger wheel well.
Clutch slip test and dual-mass flywheel chatter.
Fender replacement: panel gaps, paint-meter readings, and front structure and strut tower condition.
Underbody corrosion on the subframe, floors, jack points and brake lines (Northeast car).
Full module scan: VANOS/valvetronic adaptations, eccentric-shaft sensor, DSC.
Camber plates and top mounts, B4 dampers, thrust-arm and control-arm bushings.
Dealer check of open recalls by VIN.
Exhaust hangers and joints around the muffler-delete pipe.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: receipts showing a water pump and thermostat within ~50k miles, plus dated gasket-job invoices.
Up: a clean independent PPI in Connecticut before the close, with no leaks, no codes and a sound underbody.
Down: evidence of coolant loss, rust on the subframe or floors, or a poor-quality front-structure repair.
Down: the hammer running well above ~$15k, or the seller declining a PPI.
evidence.mission_note: A manual N52 128i is exactly the profile's primary enthusiast bridge, and resale in 6-24 months should be easy. The undocumented cooling system is the item that matters most, given the 335i's coolant failure.
evidence.rationale: The VIN, window sticker and photos establish a factory six-speed manual 2011 128i Sport in Montego Blue over Terracotta. It has a clean-title claim and a Carfax summary showing 27 service records and no reported damage. The seller discloses a parking-lot fender replacement plus cosmetic flaws: cracked quarter-panel paint, a skirt scrape and hood chips. The Carfax also notes an open 2023 recall. An extensive N52 oil-sealing and VANOS catch-up is claimed with records reportedly included, but those receipts are not examined here. The electric water pump, thermostat and expansion tank are never mentioned at 153k miles. Modifications are OEM-plus and reversible, with the factory parts included, though the muffler delete and airbox need reverting for California. The main open questions are cooling history, underbody corrosion after a Northeast life, clutch condition, and whether a PPI can happen before the Sept 30 close.
evidence.next_action: Before the auction closes, ask the seller to post water pump/thermostat and gasket-job receipts and to allow an independent BMW PPI near South Glastonbury.
